title: probe attenuation and query-cost tradeoffs for inference telemetry
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a lightweight, implementable plan for probe attenuation: how we reduce sampling intensity for probes and traces as system query-cost pressure increases, without losing signal for latency/cold-cache regressions.
- Define metric ownership, dashboard gating rules, and concrete widgets to help oncall triage on cost-constrained days.

Context / motivation:
- We keep hitting a telemetry budget ceiling on high-traffic days; full trace capture becomes prohibitively expensive (query cost + storage).
- Current sampling policies are binary (on/off or fixed-rate). We need a smoothly degrading sampling policy tied to observable system load and token-cost budgets.
- Operator needs: keep SLO-sensitive traces (canaries, errors, tail-latency) while attenuating lower-value traces (successful short requests, cached hits).

Design goals (prioritized):
1) Preserve high-fidelity traces for: 95/99/99.9th latency slices, error events, rollout canary traffic, and a rotating set of evaluation prompts.
2) Reduce cost by ~30% on telemetry-heavy days with minimal loss of actionable signal. Set a budget guardrail that automatically lowers sampling when query-cost > threshold.
3) Make attenuation explainable: dashboards should show what was attenuated and why (policy + recent actions).
4) Keep operator controls simple: one knob for budget mode (normal, conservative, emergency) and one per-tenant override.

Key concepts / vocabulary (use consistently):
- Probe: synthetic or instrumented check that emits metric + optional trace.
- Attenuation: reduction in sample rate, trace detail, or retention horizon. (We prefer deliberate wording instead of "throttling" so operators know telemetry still runs.)
- Budget band: three-tier thresholds (green, amber, red) computed from 7-day rolling query-cost and current ingestion cost.
- Signal weight: a small integer tag attached at ingestion time (1=must-capture, 2=prefer, 3=best-effort).

Proposed attenuation policy (sketch):
- Input signals: current telemetry ingestion rate (tokens/day), active query-cost (tokens/tokenized-cost), SLO burn-rate, and mitigation flags (deploy in progress, major incident).
- Band calculation:
  * Green: ingestion < 75% of budget -> sampling unchanged (baseline).
  * Amber: 75-95% -> attenuate best-effort traces by 5x. Reduce full-span capture for requests with length < 128 tokens and no error by dropping expensive span annotations (e.g., kernel-selection payloads).
  * Red: >95% -> further attenuate by 10x; preserve only weight=1 signals and a 1% reservoir sample of weight=2. Also trim retention to 3 days for weight=2 traces, 14 days for weight=1.
- Emergency: manual toggle that forces sampling down to weight=1 only and enables short-term retention compression.

Sampling heuristics (examples):
- Error-first: any request that produces non-2xx or model-hallucination-tag -> full trace regardless of band.
- Latency-slice-based up-sampling: dynamic bump for requests above p95 latency in the last 5m window.
- KV-cache cold path: when cold-cache is detected for a tenant, escalate to full trace for next N requests (N configurable, default 50).
- Canaries and evals: always weight=1 (never attenuate).

Metric definitions to add/update (short form):
- telemetry.ingest.tokens_per_minute: gauge, tokens entering telemetry pipeline per minute. Owner: metrics-eng.
- telemetry.cost.rate: gauge, estimated $ cost per hour of telemetry ingestion (based on query-cost * storage unit). Owner: eng-observability.
- telemetry.sampling.band: discrete enum (green|amber|red|emergency). Owner: eng-observability.
- telemetry.trace.captured.count_by_weight: counter, counts traces captured broken by signal_weight. Owner: eng-observability.
- telemetry.trace.dropped.count: counter, traces dropped due to attenuation. Owner: eng-observability.
- operator.override.sampling: gauge, 0/1 flag per tenant. Owner: platform-ops.

Tracing notes / span design adjustments (to reduce payload size):
- Trim large attributes at ingestion: drop full prompt payload unless request flagged as eval/canary/error. Store prompt hash + length.
- Kernel-selection and quantization-metadata: move into an optional secondary span only captured for weight=1. For weight=2/3 capture only an opcode id.
- Batch-level spans: collapse micro-spans (token-level kernel calls) into a single batch span with aggregated stats for weight>1.

Dashboard wireframe (minimum viable widgets):
- Top-level telemetry budget panel: current band, 7d trend, projected burn line. (Single row on ops frontboard).
- Sampling composition donut: traces by weight (1/2/3) + dropped %. Drilldown link to tenant-level view.
- Cost vs latency correlation scatter: x=telemetry cost delta, y=p99 latency delta, point per tenant last 24h.
- Recent attenuation actions timeline: when attenuation changed bands + operator triggers + overrides (clickable to open audit log).
- Fast debug mini-dashboard: recent error traces (weight=1) with search by prompt-hash, tenant, model.

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall):
- If band turns amber: check top heavy tenants (cost vs token rate), recommend temporary per-tenant overrides or reduce probe frequency for synthetic checks.
- If band turns red: prioritize by SLO-critical tenants. Engage infra to check ingestion pump/backpressure. Consider enabling emergency fallback (weight=1 only) for 15m and run selective replays for missed traces later.
- Post-mortem questions: did attenuation mask a root-cause trace? Were KV cold-cache regressions missed? Add specific replay hooks if yes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute telemetry.cost.rate with acceptable accuracy? (pricing model: storage + egress + query compute). Action: finance + platform to propose model (INF-3421).
- Should signal_weight be extensible per-team via API? (pros: flexible; cons: complexity). Proposal: start fixed, evolve after 1 quarter.
- Data retention policy for attenuated traces: compressed vs truncated JSON vs aggregated metrics? Need storage diff estimate.
- UX: operator-level explanation string when attenuation occurs -> one-liner recommended. Owner: product-observability.
- Experiment plan: run amber policy in canary for 2 weeks with full audit logs + synthetic regression suite. If false-negative rate for regression detection < 5% continue rollout.

Quick action items (assignments):
- Maya: draft PR with sampling policy config + basic policy engine stub (github PR target: telemetry/PR/198). Due: 2024-10-04.
- Liam: add telemetry.ingest.tokens_per_minute metric + dashboard plumbing. Due: 2024-10-11.
- Sofia: cost model proposal with finance, include storage delta estimates for trimmed traces. Due: 2024-10-18.
- Product (assigned): add operator UX strings and gating controls in console.

Notes to self / low-fidelity experiments to run locally:
- Simulate variable token load with synthetic generator, run our baseline sampler vs attenuation policy and measure retained p95-p99 error detection.
- Replay a past incident ingestion and see what traces would have been kept/dropped.

References and inspiration:
- Slack thread: #ops-telemetry 2024-09-20 (long discussion on sampling cost).
- INF-2422 (previous probe-runbook) - see for existing probe list.
- GitHub PR: telemetry/PR/145 (batch-span collapsing experiment).

Appendix: sample config sketch (human-readable):
- telemetry_budget: 1_000_000_tokens_per_day
- policy:
    baseline_rate: 1.0
    amber_rate_multiplier: 0.2
    red_rate_multiplier: 0.1
    weight_preserve: [1]
    emergency_mode_ttl_minutes: 15

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally rough. The goal is to push a small, auditable attenuation prototype into the telemetry sandbox and run the statistical safety tests.
- Keep notes here as we iterate; final spec will be moved to confluence and product docs once stable.
